gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many pixels each sub-$200 four-channel camera records per set of frames (Botslab G980H about 10.9 MP, REDTIGER F17 Plus about 9.9 MP, four-1080p models about 8.3 MP), or that the LAMTTO DC25's 2.5K mode records fewer total pixels (about 7.6 MP) than its own four-1080p mode.
standout_why: Compared against milewitness.com and truepicked.com (both opened): neither lists a four-channel camera, a bitrate or a GB-per-hour figure; truepicked only says a 128 GB card 'stores 12+ hours' for 1080p cameras in general. Our own dealectric.com/best-4-channel-dash-cam (rank 8 in chat 1) already carries the one full hours-per-card derivation I could source: F17 Plus, 46 Mbps, about 20.7 GB per hour, about 6.2 hours on its 128 GB card. I could not source a bitrate or a maker hours-per-card figure for the Rexing C4, Botslab G980H or either LAMTTO, because rexing.com and botslab.com returned HTTP 429 on every attempt and lamtto.com product pages did too. What is new is therefore only the pixel arithmetic and the price per channel, which is part of the angle, not the hours figure it was meant to deliver.
decides: It confirms rather than decides. Among cameras at or under $200 on 2026-11-21, the Botslab G980H through our link ($192.70 with code AA18) records the most pixels per set of frames: about 31% more than a four-1080p camera, with a front camera at 2.25 times the pixels of a 1080p front. That supports it as the pick for front, rear, left and right coverage over the Rexing C4 (four 1080p, $199.99 as carried on our existing page). The REDTIGER F17 Plus ($189.99) is the under-$200 row for front, two cabin views and rear, and it is the only candidate with a sourced loop length. The LAMTTO DC25 takes cards only up to 128 GB, and its 2.5K mode drops two cameras to 720p. Caution for the lead: our existing 4-channel page lists the Botslab G980H under 'Not recommended' with no price; check why before making it the pick here.
